spans.author: Klein, Josh
spans.text: Hi Walle, Abby

spans.author: Klein, Josh
spans.text: I've attached the memo for the Operating in a Sustained 10% Trend Environment topic for EPGC

spans.author: Klein, Josh
spans.text: Let us know if you have feedback or need anything else

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: Thanks so much for your submission.

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: Walle and I reviewed and have a few points of feedback we'd recommend incorporating if you can share another turn of the materials by 5pm EST tomorrow

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: Reframe the paper around the four questions on the September agenda

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: What must the enterprise do differently if elevated trend persists?

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: The memo states "ETM's expanded ambition cannot be absorbed within today's cost of care funding, capacity, etc." but does not acknowledge what changes or support the broader enterprise may need to ideate or execute differently.

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: We'd recommend including additional detail about changes required to make effectively managing through elevated trend an embedded enterprise-wide capability.

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: Which pricing, product, network, benefit, operating, strategic, and investment assumptions change?

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: Which no-regret actions and contingency triggers should enter the 2027 plan now?

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: How will the enterprise exceed the relative 25-basis-point target?

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: This question in particular remains unaddressed by what was submitted.

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: Anything you can do to clarify actions, timing, confidence level, etc. would be helpful.

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: If we can't answer yet, provide some clarity about what is still outstanding.

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: Reinforce what the September EPGC must decide; ETM was already approved in August.

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: We would not recommend too much re-emphasis on this as a decision point.

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: It is fine to remind folks of what was already decided as part of the total response to elevated trend, but we recommend re-emphasizing new approvals, funding, scope, priorities, or accepted risks required on September 24.

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: Define the proposed BEPMM decision.

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: It is unclear what scope, funding, timing, owner, expected result, or changes are implied with that decision.

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: Clarify how the five longer-term strategic moves were determined:

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: Market intelligence

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: Data

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: Competitor insights

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: Add measurable triggers—for example, sustained trend, margin, utilization, affordability, membership, or market signals—and state what strategic action each trigger activates.

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: Reduce the four-page main body to two pages, three pages maximum.

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: Feel free to move background and longer descriptions of the five strategic moves to an appendix to make the memo body more concise.

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text:
Feel free to reach out to me or Walle with any questions or clarifications. Thanks again for your work!

Abby

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: Just wanted to follow up to check in on timing for your next turn of the memo

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: We're reviewing pre-reads with Mark tomorrow late morning

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text: If you can let me know if we should expect another turn by that time, I'd appreciate it very much

spans.author: Milloy, Abby
spans.text:
Thank you!
Abby

spans.text: Here you go.

spans.text: Big thanks to this group on the email for the quick turnaround on this.

spans.author: Weber, Kyle

spans.author: Ali, Kanwal (Walle)
spans.text: Thanks for the revisions to the memo

spans.author: Ali, Kanwal (Walle)
spans.text: We just met with Mark and have a couple more points of feedback

spans.author: Ali, Kanwal (Walle)
spans.text: We'd appreciate it if you can send back final versions of the memo(s) to us by 10am EST Monday

spans.author: Ali, Kanwal (Walle)
spans.text: Split this memo into two separate memos. First with the assumptions and long-term strategy and second with the immediate leadership actions/decisions

spans.author: Ali, Kanwal (Walle)
spans.text: For the discussion, start with the assumptions and long-term strategy memo to get agreement from the Council on the approach, assumptions and five strategic areas to pressure test

spans.author: Ali, Kanwal (Walle)
spans.text: My push on the five areas of focus as they are currently framed out, is that we need to validate whether these are the right areas using actual historical experience from commercial, government, and Carelon on where we have tried some of these strategies, where they have or have not worked, and what would be different this time

spans.author: Ali, Kanwal (Walle)
spans.text: Speaking from firsthand experience building/launching several of these in Commercial

spans.author: Ali, Kanwal (Walle)
Ali, Kanwal (Walle)
spans.text: Clarify upfront what work we have completed since the decision was made in August

spans.author: Ali, Kanwal (Walle)
spans.text: For the budgeted positions ask, produce a table for CoC, MCCC, and ETM (separated out by each) that shows the expense ($) and number of positions supporting each work stream for 2024, 2025, 2026, and 2027 (projection)

spans.author: Ali, Kanwal (Walle)
spans.text: We are seeking to understand the trajectory of expense across this work

spans.author: Ali, Kanwal (Walle)
spans.text: For the proposed funding reallocation for BEPMM, confirm that Ratnakar is aligned with this ask

spans.author: Ali, Kanwal (Walle)
spans.text: Please reach out with any questions

spans.author: Tanal, Stephen
spans.text: Ratnakar, we are working to finalize the EPGC memo related to Enterprise Trend Management

spans.author: Tanal, Stephen
spans.text: including the recommendation to pursue further development of capabilities to predict and manage benefit expense in one coordinated project (Benefit Expense Projection & Management Modernization) funded by allocations from multiple projects requiring related capabilities (Member Orchestration, Medical Cost Command Center, HealthOS, etc.)

spans.author: Tanal, Stephen
spans.text: We would like to confirm whether you are aligned with this recommendation as well, per the highlight below and the callout in the memo attached

spans.author: Tanal, Stephen
spans.text:
Thank you,
Steve

spans.author: Lavu, Ratnakar
spans.text: Thanks for sharing this with me.

spans.author: Lavu, Ratnakar
spans.text: I have been talking to the various teams that you have been working with - member orchestration, CoC, Clinical Intelligence.

spans.author: Lavu, Ratnakar
spans.text: They all believe this should not be a separate set of work, but should be integrated into the work that's being done.

spans.author: Lavu, Ratnakar
spans.text: For example, the Clinical Intelligence platform will have the ability to have predictive, reactive, and realtime models and algorithms.

spans.author: Lavu, Ratnakar
spans.text: ML models as well as Gen AI models.

spans.author: Lavu, Ratnakar
spans.text: Those will then be used for CoC, Member Orchestration, and any other use cases.

spans.author: Lavu, Ratnakar
spans.text: I also comeback to us working together to build these models out versus you hiring resources to do it independently as they all need to be deployed into production leveraging common platforms that we are building out for the enterprise.

spans.author: Lavu, Ratnakar
spans.text: My recommendation is to change the below paragraph to ask for approval to make this a priority, and Strategic Finance and Technology will work together to allocate the right capacity to accomplish the work while integrating into the enterprise ecosystem.

spans.author: Lavu, Ratnakar
spans.text:
Thanks
Ratnakar

Approve Benefit Expense Projection & Management Modernization (BEPMM). Approve the proposed $15.0M one-time 2027 investment and $4.65M annual run rate to modernize benefit-expense projections and management, including a common Trend Advantage methodology, forward-looking forecasts and glidepaths, trend-driver attribution, and Finance-certified value measurement and prioritization. Funding is proposed through reallocation from existing initiatives that require these capabilities, with Strategic Finance as business owner and governance lead, working in close collaboration with Health Solutions, Health Outcomes Organization and DPAIO

spans.author: Tanal, Stephen
spans.text: Ratnakar, thanks for your quick response and readiness to partner on the work.

spans.author: Tanal, Stephen
spans.text: I want to clarify that we appear to be focused on the same critical goal

spans.author: Tanal, Stephen
spans.text: not making any of this work “a separate set of work.”

spans.author: Tanal, Stephen
spans.text: The purpose of the BEPMM proposal is in fact to coordinate and track the work that is being done and integrate parallel workstreams wherever it makes sense.

spans.author: Tanal, Stephen
spans.text: The example you raise is a case in point – what exactly is the Clinical Intelligence platform and how is it being funded?

spans.author: Tanal, Stephen
spans.text: Is that a standalone SVRO project today?

spans.author: Tanal, Stephen
spans.text: Given that the capabilities you describe as being a part of this will be used for CoC, Member Orchestration and any other use cases (e.g. HealthOS/TMV), how do you propose we ensure transparency, lack of duplication of work and funding, and the appropriate degree of enterprise focus, if not by bringing all related work in one place (BEPMM)?

spans.author: Tanal, Stephen
spans.text: I also want to make clear my team has no intention of doing any end-to-end work independently.

spans.author: Tanal, Stephen
spans.text: We are 100% aligned with deploying into production through DPAIO leveraging common platforms.

spans.author: Tanal, Stephen
spans.text: My team would, however, like to ensure iterative ML/AI model development occurs close to our Actuarial and Finance SMEs who drive our predictive capabilities today, with embedded data scientists working closely together day-to-day.

spans.author: Tanal, Stephen
spans.text: This is what Strategic Finance uniquely offers to the cross-functional working group.

spans.author: Tanal, Stephen
spans.text:
Thank you,
Steve

spans.author: Lavu, Ratnakar
spans.text: Thanks Steve. What is BEPMM?

spans.author: Lavu, Ratnakar
spans.text: Is it a capability or a governing body?

spans.author: Lavu, Ratnakar

## The main point

Abby Milloy and Kanwal Ali, who reviewed the Enterprise Trend Management memo with Mark, are asking an unidentified author to revise and resubmit materials by 10am EST Monday. Abby wants the memo reframed around four specific September agenda questions, condensed from four pages to two or three, and clarified on what the EPGC must decide in September versus what was already approved in August. Kanwal adds that the memo should be split into two documents — one on assumptions and long-term strategy, one on immediate decisions — and wants a table showing headcount and expense for CoC, MCCC, and ETM across 2024 through 2027, as well as validation that the five strategic focus areas are grounded in actual historical experience from commercial, government, and Carelon. Both Abby and Kanwal flag that the BEPMM proposal is unclear on scope, funding, timing, owner, and expected result. Stephen Tanal asked Ratnakar Lavu directly whether he is aligned with the proposed BEPMM funding reallocation; Ratnakar did not align, saying the teams he has spoken with believe the work should be integrated into existing programs rather than run as a separate workstream, and proposed changing the ask to one for prioritization with Strategic Finance and Technology jointly allocating capacity. Stephen pushed back, saying BEPMM is intended to coordinate parallel workstreams rather than create independent work, but Stephen and Ratnakar remain unresolved on whether BEPMM should exist as a distinct project at all and on who should provide data science resources — meaning the $15.0M one-time 2027 investment and $4.65M annual run-rate request cannot move forward without that being settled before the September EPGC meeting.

## Presented, no challenge recorded

- ETM was already approved in August and is not the September decision point; the September meeting should re-emphasize new approvals, funding, scope, priorities, or accepted risks (Abby Milloy).
